claims.text: Residual internal micro-strains dominate the magnetocaloric response of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy nanostructures under low-field cycling.
Edge-induced defect sites dominate hysteresis in these nanostructures during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Low-temperature annealing relieves residual micro-strain in these nanostructures.
Low-temperature annealing reduces edge-imperfection or defect density in these nanostructures.
Residual micro-strain and edge-induced defects act as magnetic-domain pinning centers.
Internal strain heterogeneity creates spatial variations in magnetic exchange interactions.
Internal strain heterogeneity enhances domain-wall pinning.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning broadens the magnetic transition.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning increases magnetic hysteresis.
Annealing-induced strain and defect reduction produces more uniform magnetic interactions.
Annealed samples will exhibit a sharper and more uniform magnetic transition than as-deposited samples.
Annealed samples will exhibit less hysteresis than as-deposited samples.
Annealing will improve effective cycle frequency within heat-transfer constraints.
The proposed mechanism applies to films below approximately 200 nm in thickness or comparably sized patterned nanoribbons.
Heat-transfer rates limit the applicable magnetic-cycling frequency.
The proposed mechanism may not extend to thicker films or bulk samples because strain and defect effects differ.
